evidence.observation: In the child-allow-agent arm the parent's Agent call started a general-purpose sub-agent whose own Bash tool_use blocks appeared in the stream tagged with the parent's tool_use id.

tool-isolation.reason: Not re-measured on 2.1.282. The contract capability concerns an agent definition's `tools:` restriction, measured only on 2.1.220 (see that record). This run measured session-level tool availability (`--tools`) and permission approval, which are recorded under `observations` and do not decide this capability.

model-selection.reason: No model-selection probe was run on 2.1.282; the 2.1.220 measurement does not carry to another version.

fresh-context.reason: No fresh-context probe was run on 2.1.282; the 2.1.220 measurement does not carry to another version.

workspace-isolation.reason: No probe has tested whether the runtime provides a separate writable workspace per task.

observations.summary: Permission approval applied equally to a parent session and to the general-purpose sub-agent it spawned, under --permission-mode default with no allow rules in user settings. Calls outside `--allowedTools` were refused unless the runtime classified them as read-only.

evidence.observation: With --allowedTools Read (parent) and Agent,Read (child): Bash `git --version` and `echo … > file` returned is_error=true and no file was written, in both the parent and the child; Bash `git status --short && find … -print` returned is_error=false in both, so the runtime auto-approved it as read-only. --allowedTools pre-approves calls; it does not remove tools from the session.

observations.summary: `--tools Agent,Read` removed Bash from the session's tool list; the spawned child emitted no Bash call and no file was written.

evidence.observation: In the child-tools-agent arm the parent init listed no Bash tool, the child produced no Bash tool_use, and childtools.txt was not created. No refusal was observed because no call was made, so this is availability, not enforcement.
